headline: Consumer choices shape your life and the world—every purchase is a vote for what you value
universal_truth: You vote with your money; what you buy reflects and reinforces what you value
fun_facts: The average person makes thousands of consumer decisions each year
Marketing is designed to create desire—awareness helps you choose rather than react
Buying less but better often costs less and satisfies more over time
discussion_questions: How deliberately do you make purchasing decisions?
Do your purchases align with your values?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Every purchase is a choice. Not just about what you get, but about what you support, what you value, how you spend limited resources. In a consumer world, choosing what to buy is choosing how to live.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: It's easy to buy impulsively or follow marketing. Why does thoughtful consumption matter?

options.text: Choices compound—each purchase uses resources, supports companies, fills your life with things; mindless buying creates clutter, debt, and misalignment; deliberate choice means intentional life
options.response: Yes. Your purchases shape your environment, your finances, your time, and the world. Every dollar is a vote. Spending thoughtlessly means living thoughtlessly. Choose consciously.
Sometimes, but often the happiness is brief while the stuff remains; experiences and values tend to satisfy longer...

q1.title: Want vs Need
q1.script: Distinguish wants from needs. Both are valid, but confusing them leads to poor choices. Know when you're meeting necessity versus desire. Neither is wrong; clarity is essential.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Want vs Need"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Marketing Awareness
q2.script: You're constantly targeted by marketing designed to create desire. Being aware of manipulation helps you choose rather than react. Notice when you want something because you were told to want it.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Total Cost
q3.script: The price tag isn't the total cost. Maintenance, storage, time, environmental impact—all factor in. Cheap things that break cost more than quality that lasts. Consider true cost.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You vote with your money. What you buy reflects and reinforces what you value. Choose deliberately.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 342. Tomorrow, we'll explore sharing what you have—generosity. Until then, notice what influences your purchases.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Purchase Audit - What Are You Buying?
growTrack.activity: Review recent purchases. How many were deliberate versus impulsive? Do they align with your values? What did you buy that you regret? What would more conscious consumption look like?
